title: Write a shippable prompt brief
summary: You'll turn a vague feature idea into a brief an agent can execute without guessing.
lesson: A good brief states the user, the job-to-be-done, and what done looks like.
Include constraints: stack, files you may touch, and what not to invent.
Add one acceptance check the agent can verify (route loads, test passes, form submits).
Prefer concrete nouns over vibes: “POST /api/events returns 202” beats “make it work.”

choices: Make the learning app cooler with AI vibes.
Add /launch that verifies a Ludwitt JWT and redirects to /learn when valid.
Use best practices for auth somehow.
quiz.explain: It names the route, the verification step, and the success redirect.

quiz.prompt: What should a brief tell the agent not to do?
choices: Invent deploy URLs or peer data that were not verified.

title: Instrument learning events
summary: You'll know which learning events to fire so sessions count toward platform metrics.
lesson: Launch creates a session id you reuse for every event in that visit.
Fire lesson_started when a module opens — not only on page load of marketing.
Fire quiz_submitted when the learner answers; include score in metadata if useful.
Fire lesson_completed when the module summary is reached. Heartbeats alone do not qualify a session.

quiz.prompt: Minimum non-heartbeat signal for a valid learning session?
choices: At least one of lesson_started, quiz_submitted, or lesson_completed
quiz.explain: Platform pass evidence requires real learning events, not heartbeats alone.

quiz.prompt: Where should the Ludwitt api_key live?
quiz.explain: Browser exposure would let anyone spoof events as your app.

title: Trust the Ludwitt launch JWT
summary: You'll validate launch tokens and reject anything that did not come from the launcher.
lesson: Ludwitt redirects to your /launch?token=… with a short-lived HS256 JWT.
Verify signature with jwt_secret, check exp, and confirm app_id matches your registration.
On failure, show “Launch from Ludwitt” — do not silently create a guest that looks launched.
Store sub/email/session in an httpOnly cookie; never put api_key in that cookie.

choices: Be rejected with a clear launch-from-platform message
quiz.explain: Invalid tokens must not grant a learning session.

quiz.prompt: JWT payload field that identifies the Ludwitt user?
quiz.explain: sub is the platform user id used in event user_id.

title: Ship as part of a suite
summary: You'll connect learning to Market, PM, and Chat without fake SSO claims.
lesson: EudaLearn is the Phase 2 learning surface; EudaPM, EudaChat, and EudaMarket already cover work, chat, and showcase.
Deep-link from Market /suite so partners and peers can find the app — but counted users should enter via the Ludwitt listing/launcher.
Be honest about auth: Ludwitt JWT for launched sessions; per-host cookies elsewhere.
Promote the listing URL in cohort channels so later snapshots can measure adoption.
One suite story beats four orphan demos: same brand, clear handoffs, no invented shared login.

choices: Only the raw Vercel URL in a private gist
quiz.explain: Launcher entry is what ties users to platform metrics.

quiz.prompt: What should you avoid claiming across EudaMarket, EudaPM, EudaChat, and EudaLearn?
choices: That they share branding and deep links
That they are one product suite for the pilot
That they share a single SSO session cookie across every host
That learners should prefer the Ludwitt listing for counted use
quiz.explain: Auth is per host / Ludwitt launch — do not invent cross-app SSO.
